SpectrumExplorer.Load Target FITS…: Opens a file browser to load the target FITS frame to analyse. Loading a new file resets the current analysis (detected sources, calibration overlays, continuum anchors) but keeps the configuration (angle, dispersion, nodes), which is applied automatically — no need to press UPDATE.
SpectrumExplorer.Start Livestack: Watches a folder and stacks its FITS frames live: files already in the folder are stacked first, then each new arrival is registered onto the first (reference) frame and added; the pipeline re-runs on the growing stack with the selected source kept active. Click again (“Stop Livestack”) to stop watching; the accumulated stack stays loaded.
SpectrumExplorer.Legacy response: Two-column instrument-response file (wavelength, response factor) used to flatten the extracted spectrum — for curves produced externally or by “Calibrate instrument response…” in an earlier session. Editing this path invalidates any response curve embedded in a loaded config so the file is re-read fresh on the next Run.
SpectrumExplorer.Load config…: Loads a previously saved analysis config (calibration file/array, angle, dispersion, y-offset, dispersion nodes) and re-runs the pipeline with it.
SpectrumExplorer.Save config…: Saves the current calibration file, angle, dispersion, y-offset and non-linear dispersion nodes to a JSON config file for reuse.
SpectrumExplorer.▶ AUTO-DEROT. and PROC: Detects the spectrum tilt automatically (using the selected first-pass method below, refined by a second pass on the extracted strip), fills in Rotation angle, and runs a full extraction. Use when you don't know the tilt angle for this setup yet.
SpectrumExplorer.first_pass_method: Chooses the whole-frame detector used by Auto-derotate's first pass. “FFT (single pass)” (default) is usually the most accurate and skips the second refinement pass; “Statistical Hough” and “Coherence” are alternatives that also get a strip-based refinement pass unless they fail.
SpectrumExplorer.Rot. angle: Frame rotation, in degrees, applied before extraction so the spectrum runs horizontally. Set manually or via Auto-derotate; the −/+ buttons nudge it by 0.05° and re-run.
SpectrumExplorer.angle_minus: Decreases the rotation angle by 0.05° and re-runs extraction.
SpectrumExplorer.angle_plus: Increases the rotation angle by 0.05° and re-runs extraction.
SpectrumExplorer.N sources: Maximum number of point sources DAOStarFinder will detect in the frame. Default 10; raise it for crowded fields where the target isn't among the brightest sources found.
SpectrumExplorer.FWHM (px): Expected stellar PSF full-width-half-maximum, in pixels, passed to DAOStarFinder for source detection and used to auto-size the extraction aperture and background-gap on a fresh source switch. Match it to the actual seeing/focus; too small misses sources, too large merges close pairs.
SpectrumExplorer.Å / px: Linear dispersion of the spectrum, in Å per pixel, used as the fallback wavelength solution when fewer than two calibration nodes exist and as the base scale for the secondary axis in the calibration dialogs. Typical value for this instrument is ~7.7 Å/px; refine with the dispersion calibration dialog once enough nodes are placed.
SpectrumExplorer.λ min (Å): Lower wavelength bound (Å) of the displayed/extracted spectral range. Sets the left edge of the plotted spectrum panels.
SpectrumExplorer.λ max (Å): Upper wavelength bound (Å) of the displayed/extracted spectral range. Sets the right edge of the plotted spectrum panels.
SpectrumExplorer.Aper half-h: Half-height, in pixels, of the extraction aperture centred on the source row. The aperture spans 2×this+1 rows. Auto-sized to ~0.83×FWHM on a fresh source switch; raise it to capture more flux from a bloated/defocused source, lower it to reduce contamination from nearby sources.
SpectrumExplorer.Bkg Hi gap: Gap, in pixels, between the top of the extraction aperture and the background (sky) band above it, so the wings of the source PSF aren't included in the background estimate. Auto-sized to ~0.7×FWHM on a fresh source switch. The high and low bands are independent: in a crowded field, widen the gap on the side a contaminator sits.
SpectrumExplorer.Bkg Lo gap: Gap, in pixels, between the bottom of the extraction aperture and the background (sky) band below it, so the wings of the source PSF aren't included in the background estimate. Auto-sized to ~0.7×FWHM on a fresh source switch. The high and low bands are independent: in a crowded field, widen the gap on the side a contaminator sits.
SpectrumExplorer.width: Width, in pixels, of this background (sky) band — the rows sampled to estimate and subtract the local background level.
SpectrumExplorer.Y offset: Vertical pixel offset applied to the extraction row, on top of the detected source centroid. Use the −/+ buttons to nudge the extraction position and re-extract without changing the detected source.
SpectrumExplorer.aper_minus: Decreases the strip y offset by one pixel and re-extracts.
SpectrumExplorer.aper_plus: Increases the strip y offset by one pixel and re-extracts.
SpectrumExplorer.Auto center: When on (the default), every new extraction — Run, source switch, free click — is automatically centred on the trace. The ± nudges and display toggles are left alone, so a manual offset is not undone the moment you set it. These shifts do not mark the config as needing a save: the offset is re-derived per source rather than chosen by you.
SpectrumExplorer.centre_on_trace: Tries the strip at each y offset within ±5 pixels and keeps the one that extracts the most spectrum — the aperture is on the trace when it captures the most light. Only the λ min–λ max columns are scored, so the zero-order star is ignored: on bright stars that blob is saturated and is exactly what pulls the detected centroid off. Reports the shift it made and warns if the best offset was at the edge of its search, in which case click again. Mostly useful with Auto center off, which is when it highlights — with autocentring on, every new extraction has already been centred and the button is redundant.
SpectrumExplorer.Mask in-aperture stars: When on, NaN-masks spectrum columns where another detected source's PSF overlaps the extraction aperture, removing that contaminant's flux from the result instead of leaving it blended in. Contaminants are matched against every star found on the frame — including ones a FWHM outside the band, whose wings still reach in — rather than re-detected inside the strip, where a half-in star never shows the whole PSF a detector needs. Off by default.
SpectrumExplorer.Free selection (click any point): When on, a left-click anywhere on the working image extracts a spectrum from that exact pixel instead of snapping to the nearest DAOStarFinder-detected source. Useful for faint companions or arbitrary points (e.g. a nebula) not in the detected source list.
SpectrumExplorer.Zero-order wavelength anchor: When on, the dispersion solution (calibrated on one star) is re-anchored to each source's own measured zero-order peak, cancelling a colour-dependent centroid offset that otherwise shifts the wavelength scale by a fraction of a pixel between stars of different colour. Leave on for cross-star consistency; turning it off reproduces the older, uncorrected behaviour.
SpectrumExplorer.▶ UPDATE: Re-runs extraction and display with the current parameter-panel values, without re-detecting the rotation angle.
SpectrumExplorer.Calibrate dispersion…: Opens the dispersion calibration dialog to add, edit or auto-suggest pixel-to-wavelength nodes for a non-linear wavelength solution (used instead of the flat Å/px value once ≥2 nodes exist).
SpectrumExplorer.Calibrate instrument response…: Opens the instrument-response calibration dialog, which derives a response (flat-field) curve from an observed A0V star compared to a reference template.
SpectrumExplorer.Calibrate continuum…: Opens the continuum dialog to place anchor points that define the spectrum's smooth baseline, for continuum-subtracted or continuum-normalised views.
SpectrumExplorer.Plot Balmer lines: Overlays reference marker lines for the hydrogen Balmer series on the spectrum plots. On by default.
SpectrumExplorer.Plot Helium lines: Overlays reference marker lines for Helium lines on the spectrum plots. Off by default.
SpectrumExplorer.Plot atmospheric lines: Overlays reference marker lines for telluric (atmospheric absorption) bands on the spectrum plots. On by default.
SpectrumExplorer.Plot Oxygen lines: Overlays reference marker lines for Oxygen lines on the spectrum plots. Off by default.
SpectrumExplorer.Plot Carbon lines: Overlays reference marker lines for Carbon lines on the spectrum plots. Off by default.
SpectrumExplorer.Plot Carbon Star lines: Overlays reference marker lines for carbon-star molecular bands on the spectrum plots. Off by default.
SpectrumExplorer.Plot WR WN lines: Overlays reference marker lines for Wolf-Rayet WN-type emission lines on the spectrum plots. Off by default.
SpectrumExplorer.Plot WR WC lines: Overlays reference marker lines for Wolf-Rayet WC-type emission lines on the spectrum plots. Off by default.
SpectrumExplorer.Show calibration lines: Overlays vertical markers at the currently placed dispersion-calibration node wavelengths, for visual reference. Display only — does not affect the fit.
SpectrumExplorer.▶ Animate: Opens the sequence generator, which extracts and animates the calibrated spectrum across a folder of tracked FITS frames using the current analysis parameters.
SpectrumExplorer.⤢ View full spectrum: Opens a full-size, resizable view of the calibrated & normalised spectrum with continuum overlay, uncertainty band and export controls.
SpectrumExplorer.⤢ View active response curve…: Opens a read-only plot of the instrument-response curve currently in use (the array embedded in a loaded config, or the file in the Legacy response field).
SpectrumExplorer.⤢ Browse reference library…: Opens a browser over the local Pickles reference spectra library, with a search box to filter by spectral type.
SpectrumExplorer.ASTAP: Path to the ASTAP executable used for plate-solving the working frame. Persisted in the analysis config since it's machine-specific.
SpectrumExplorer.✦ Solve to WCS: Plate-solves the current working (rotated) frame with ASTAP, then cross-matches each detected source against SIMBAD by sky position, populating the source-identification info box below and enabling “Check SIMBAD” / “LAMOST” for the selected source.
SpectrumExplorer.↗ Check SIMBAD: Opens the SIMBAD web page for the currently selected source's resolved catalog identifier. Disabled until a WCS solve has matched the selection to a catalog entry.
SpectrumExplorer.↗ LAMOST: Opens a viewer for the LAMOST DR11 low-resolution archival spectrum of the currently selected source, for comparison against the extracted spectrum. Disabled until a WCS solve has matched the selection to a catalog entry.
SpectrumExplorer.Show source names: Shows or hides the resolved catalog names (and spectral types) next to the detected sources on the working image. The numbered circles always stay — they are how you switch sources. On by default; only affects the display.
SpectrumExplorer.✧ Predictor: EXPERIMENTAL — opens the spectral-type predictor: ranks Pickles library templates by whole-band shape match against the current calibrated spectrum (the same comparison shown as the 4th panel in the continuum dialog). Needs a calibrated extraction and a good response correction.
SpectrumExplorer.✶ Catalogues: Target-planning catalogue browsers: Be stars (Jaschek & Egret, with an Hα-emission-chance rating), Wolf-Rayet stars (van der Hucht), bright quasars (Véron-Cetty & Véron, < mag 16), carbon stars (Alksnis+, V < 10), Mira variables (GCVS, max < 10), S-type stars (Stephenson), cataclysmic variables (Downes, max < 12 — an outburst magnitude, check recent photometry), symbiotic stars (Belczyński+) and Herbig Ae/Be & T Tauri (Herbig-Bell). All share sortable columns (click a heading), J2000 and JNOW positions, constellation, a Spec column counting spectra already in the local database, an Alt° column (the object's maximum altitude during tonight's darkness at the observer location — judge your own dome/cupola limits with it), a Visible-tonight filter (observer lat/lon, tonight's darkness window, altitude > 30°) and a Goto button that slews via the open NINA remote.
SpectrumExplorer.dispersion_calc: Opens the dispersion calculator: works out Å per pixel from your grating (lines/mm), the grating-to-sensor distance and your pixel size. Use it when you change camera, grating or spacing — the value only needs to be approximate, the wavelength calibration refines it.

CalibrationDialog.Edit selected: Reopens the wavelength-assignment panel for the selected node at its existing pixel, so you can re-pick or retype its wavelength.
CalibrationDialog.Delete selected: Removes the selected calibration node and refits the dispersion solution.
CalibrationDialog.Clear all: Deletes every calibration node after confirmation, reverting to the flat Å/px linear dispersion.
CalibrationDialog.Suggest (A-star): Automatically places calibration nodes on the Balmer absorption lines (and the 7594 Å telluric band when usable), for an A-type star with visible Balmer absorption. Replaces the current node set after a confirmation prompt if nodes already exist — review and correct any misplaced node afterwards.
CalibrationDialog.wavelength_entry: Wavelength, in Å, to assign to the clicked pixel. Pre-filled with the wavelength predicted by the current fit; overwrite with the true rest wavelength of the identified feature (or use a Quick pick button).
CalibrationDialog.Confirm: Commits the pixel/wavelength assignment as a new calibration node (or replaces an existing node at the same pixel), then refits the dispersion solution.
CalibrationDialog.Cancel: Discards the pending pixel click without adding a node.
CalibrationDialog.quick_pick_button: Fills the wavelength field with this spectral line's rest wavelength, for one-click assignment of a commonly used calibration line.

FullSpectrumViewer.Show overlay: Draws the fitted continuum curve on top of the main (rainbow-coloured) spectrum panel. Off by default so the coloured fill stays uncluttered.
FullSpectrumViewer.±2σ band: Shades a ±2σ background-noise confidence band around the main spectrum and switches its trace from the coloured RGB fill to a plain line, since the two displays are mutually exclusive. Off by default.
FullSpectrumViewer.subtract: Displays the continuum-corrected panel as flux minus continuum (baseline driven to zero). Requires ≥ 2 continuum anchors placed in the continuum dialog.
FullSpectrumViewer.normalize: Displays the continuum-corrected panel as flux divided by continuum (baseline driven to one). Requires ≥ 2 continuum anchors placed in the continuum dialog.
FullSpectrumViewer.Export FITS…: Saves the currently displayed spectrum (wavelength and flux, continuum-corrected if a mode is active) as a 1-D FITS file.

ReferenceLibraryViewer.Search:: Filters the displayed reference spectra by case-insensitive substring match on their file name (e.g. “a0v”, “b3i”). Clears to show the whole library.
ReferenceLibraryViewer.Change folder…: Chooses a different folder of reference .dat spectra to browse, replacing the default ReferenceLibrary folder.
ReferenceLibraryViewer.Reload: Re-reads all reference spectra from the current folder, picking up any files added or changed on disk since the library was last cached.

ResponseCurveViewer.Close: Closes the active response curve viewer.

ResponseCalibrationDialog.Load…: Loads a reference template spectrum (e.g. a Pickles A0V .dat file) to compare against the current extraction when computing the instrument response.
ResponseCalibrationDialog.method_selector: Chooses how the instrument-response curve is derived from the observed/reference ratio. Spline (anchors) fits a cubic spline through user-placed or auto-suggested points on the ratio — most controllable, good default. Smoothed ratio Gaussian-smooths the whole obs/ref ratio with the Balmer cores masked out, but also smooths across telluric bands. Raw (telluric-preserving) keeps the full-resolution ratio, interpolating only the Balmer cores, so telluric absorption is preserved in the response and divides out of later spectra.
ResponseCalibrationDialog.Ratio smooth FWHM (Å): Gaussian smoothing width, in Å, applied to the whole observed/reference ratio in Smoothed ratio mode. Default 400 Å. Larger values give a smoother but less detailed response; note this also smooths over telluric bands, unlike Raw mode.
ResponseCalibrationDialog.Balmer mask ±Å: Half-width, in Å, masked out around each Balmer line before computing the response, so stellar absorption cores don't get baked into the instrument response. Default 40 Å. Used by both Smoothed ratio and Raw methods, and by Auto-suggest.
ResponseCalibrationDialog.Off-telluric smooth FWHM (Å): Optional light Gaussian smoothing, in Å, applied only outside the telluric bands in Raw mode, to flatten continuum jitter without touching the preserved telluric-band depths. 0 (default) disables it.
ResponseCalibrationDialog.Recompute: Recomputes the response curve for the active method (Smoothed ratio or Raw) using the current smoothing/mask field values.
ResponseCalibrationDialog.N: (anchors): Number of anchor points Auto-suggest places on the observed/reference ratio in Spline mode. Default 12.
ResponseCalibrationDialog.Auto-suggest: Places a robust, sigma-clipped starting set of spline anchors on the observed/reference ratio (plus edge anchors covering the full range), which can then be dragged, added to or deleted.
ResponseCalibrationDialog.Clear anchors: Removes all spline anchors after confirmation.
ResponseCalibrationDialog.Save A0V spectrum…: Saves the current extraction, mapped to wavelength, as a two-column .dat file — useful for reusing the same observed A0V star later without re-extracting.
ResponseCalibrationDialog.Export response curve…: Writes the computed response curve to a two-column .dat file for use outside this config, and applies it as the live calibration. Exporting is optional — Apply alone is enough.
ResponseCalibrationDialog.Apply: Makes the computed response curve the live calibration straight away: Run uses it immediately, and Save config stores it in the config as an array. No .dat file needed.

ContinuumDialog.N: (continuum anchors): Number of anchor points Auto-suggest places along the spectrum. Default 8.
ContinuumDialog.absorption: Tells Auto-suggest to pick the higher (upper-envelope) flux value in each wavelength bin, appropriate for a spectrum with absorption features dipping below the continuum.
ContinuumDialog.emission: Tells Auto-suggest to pick the lower (lower-envelope) flux value in each wavelength bin, appropriate for a spectrum with emission features rising above the continuum.
ContinuumDialog.Suggest anchors: Places continuum anchor points automatically by picking an extreme flux value per wavelength bin (per the absorption/emission mode and N above).
ContinuumDialog.Auto-fit continuum: Fits a degree-3 Chebyshev continuum via specutils across the whole spectrum, with sigma-clipping and Balmer/telluric regions excluded, then loads N evenly-spaced points sampled from that fit as editable anchors. A statistical alternative to Suggest anchors' per-bin picking — both seed the same anchor list.
ContinuumDialog.subtract: Previews the continuum-corrected spectrum as flux minus continuum (baseline driven to zero).
ContinuumDialog.normalize: Previews the continuum-corrected spectrum as flux divided by continuum (baseline driven to one).
ContinuumDialog.Clear all: Removes all continuum anchors after confirmation.

LamostDialog.Smooth (px): Boxcar smoothing window, in pixels, applied to the archival LAMOST spectrum before display. 1 (default) applies no smoothing; odd window sizes only, up to 51 px.

SequenceGeneratorDialog.Frames folder:: Folder of tracked FITS frames to process into a spectrum sequence.
SequenceGeneratorDialog.Browse…: Chooses the frames folder to process.
SequenceGeneratorDialog.▶ Generate: Processes every FITS frame in the folder with the current analysis parameters (angle, dispersion, extraction settings) and builds the animated spectrum sequence.
SequenceGeneratorDialog.DAOStarFinder (nearest match): Positions the source in each frame by re-running DAOStarFinder and matching the nearest detection to the live source's centroid within a snap radius. Default positioning mode; works without a WCS solve.
SequenceGeneratorDialog.WCS plate solve (ASTAP): Positions the source in each frame using the main window's solved WCS (world-to-pixel of the target), instead of re-detecting by nearest centroid. Only enabled after “Solve to WCS” has been run in the main window.
SequenceGeneratorDialog.SavGol window:: Window length (odd, pixels) of the Savitzky-Golay smoothing filter applied to each frame's calibrated flux before display, to suppress noise while preserving Balmer line shape.
SequenceGeneratorDialog.polyorder:: Polynomial order used by the Savitzky-Golay smoothing filter. Must be less than the SavGol window.
SequenceGeneratorDialog.Norm pct lo/hi:: Lower/upper percentile of the flux distribution used to rescale each frame when per-frame normalisation is enabled, so that transparency variations between frames don't dominate the animation.
SequenceGeneratorDialog.Normalise each frame (neutralise transpa: When on, rescales each frame's flux independently (using the percentile range above) so that sky-transparency changes across the sequence don't show up as brightness changes, letting real spectral variation stand out. On by default.
SequenceGeneratorDialog.Save GIF…: Saves the generated animation as a GIF file. Disabled until a sequence has been generated.
SequenceGeneratorDialog.Pause: Pauses or resumes animation playback of the generated sequence. Disabled until a sequence has been generated.

NinaDialog.Host: Hostname or IP of the machine running NINA with the Advanced API plugin (the rig PC). Saved in the per-machine UI dotfile, not in the analysis config, since it's rig-specific.
NinaDialog.Port: TCP port of NINA's Advanced API (default 1888). If Connect fails, check the port on the plugin's settings page in NINA.
NinaDialog.Connect: Checks the connection in the background and reports the API version, camera/focuser connection state and the current focuser position; the camera's current gain is read into the Gain field. Run this first — nothing else in this panel works without a reachable API, and a dead host won't freeze the window.
NinaDialog.af_exp: Exposure time, in seconds, for each autofocus sweep frame. A few seconds on a bright A star gives enough Balmer-line signal to score; longer exposures just slow the sweep down.
NinaDialog.Step: Focuser steps between sweep points. The sweep spans Points × Step centred on the current focuser position — too coarse steps over the optimum, too fine wastes points measuring noise.
NinaDialog.Points: Number of focus positions measured, centred on the current focuser position. If the optimum lands on a sweep edge, the sweep auto-extends in that direction (up to 2×3 extra points).
NinaDialog.foc_step: Manual focuser control: the buttons move the focuser by this many steps from wherever it currently is — ◀ − lowers the position number, + ▶ raises it. Which way the drawtube actually travels depends on the focuser and its driver's reverse setting, so try one small step and watch. The position is re-read from NINA before each move, and the result line below reports where the focuser landed.
NinaDialog.▶ Run autofocus: Sweeps the focuser and scores the extracted spectrum at each position to find best spectral focus — chromatically offset from zero-order star focus, which is why NINA's own HFR autofocus won't land here. Point NINA at a bright A-type (Balmer-strong) star first. Runs the sweep tool as a subprocess with a snapshot of the live explorer config; click again to cancel. The pane below plots measured points, the parabola fit and best/ideal positions, plus the best frame's extracted strip once the run completes.
NinaDialog.Work folder: Local folder where captured or mirrored FITS frames are written — and the folder Livestack watches. Use a fresh (or cleaned) folder per target so leftover frames don't pollute the next stack.
NinaDialog.Find nearest: Refreshes the candidate list (it is populated automatically on Connect): reads the mount's current pointing and lists the 15 nearest Hipparcos A0-A3 stars by great-circle separation, pruned to V<4.5 so the magnitude-scaled autofocus exposure stays under 30 s. No horizon or altitude filtering is applied.
NinaDialog.Slew: Slews the mount to the selected A star after confirmation and waits for the mount to stop. This does not plate-solve or center the target.
NinaDialog.Focus run: Remembers the current mount position, slews to the selected A star, runs spectral autofocus with the exposure shown in Exp (s), and slews back after success, failure, or cancellation. Selecting a star fills Exp (s) with its forecast exposure — 3 s at V=2 scaled by the flux ratio (0.13 s on Sirius, 30 s at the V=4.5 limit) — and a hand-tweaked value is honoured.
NinaDialog.cap_exp: Exposure time, in seconds, per snapshot frame in the capture loop.
NinaDialog.Gain: Camera gain for snapshot frames, in the camera's native units. Filled with the camera's actual gain on Connect (a typed value is never overwritten); empty keeps the camera's current setting.
NinaDialog.Count (0=∞): Number of snapshot frames to take before stopping automatically. 0 keeps capturing until you press Stop.
NinaDialog.▶ Start capturing: Starts the snapshot loop: this dialog drives the camera with the exposure/gain/count above, saving each frame into the work folder. Nothing here guides or dithers — use Mirror instead when NINA's own sequence should keep control of the camera. Click again to stop after the current exposure.
NinaDialog.▶ Mirror NINA sequence: Lets NINA's own running sequence drive the camera (so guiding and dithering keep working) and polls its image history, downloading each new LIGHT frame under NINA's filename into a subfolder named after NINA's target (the work-folder field follows it, so Livestack and Cleanup act per target). Frames already in the history when mirroring starts are ignored; the local copies double as a backup of the rig files. Click again to stop.
NinaDialog.Livestack this folder: Points the explorer's livestack at the work folder: frames already there are stacked first, then each new captured/mirrored arrival is registered and added, so the spectrum builds up live while frames come in.
NinaDialog.Cleanup work folder…: Deletes every FITS file in the work folder, after a confirmation showing the count. Capture/mirror and any livestack watching this folder are stopped first. Use it between targets so the next livestack starts clean.

CameraAcquisitionWindow.Driver: ASCOM camera driver to connect to. “Simulator” requires no hardware; use the ↻ button to rescan for connected ASCOM cameras.
CameraAcquisitionWindow.driver_refresh: Rescans for available ASCOM camera drivers and refreshes the driver list.
CameraAcquisitionWindow.Connect: Connects to the selected camera driver.
CameraAcquisitionWindow.Disconnect: Disconnects from the currently connected camera.
CameraAcquisitionWindow.Gain: Camera sensor gain setting, in the camera's native units (default 100). Higher gain reduces read noise at the cost of full-well depth; check the sensor's gain table for the sweet spot.
CameraAcquisitionWindow.Offset: Camera sensor black-level offset (default 10), added to every pixel to keep read noise away from clipping at zero.
CameraAcquisitionWindow.Binning: Pixel binning factor (1–4). Higher binning trades spatial resolution for higher per-pixel signal and smaller file sizes.
CameraAcquisitionWindow.Apply sensor settings: Sends the current Gain, Offset and Binning values to the connected camera.
CameraAcquisitionWindow.Enable cooler: Turns the camera's thermoelectric cooler on or off and starts regulating toward the target temperature below.
CameraAcquisitionWindow.Target temp (°C): Setpoint temperature, in °C, for the camera cooler once enabled.
CameraAcquisitionWindow.Exposure (s): Exposure time, in seconds, for each frame in the acquisition sequence.
CameraAcquisitionWindow.Number of frames: Number of frames to capture in the sequence.
CameraAcquisitionWindow.Save directory: Folder where captured FITS frames are written.
CameraAcquisitionWindow.Filename prefix: Prefix used for each saved FITS frame's filename (frames are further distinguished by an index/timestamp).
CameraAcquisitionWindow.▶ START SEQUENCE: Begins capturing the configured number of exposures at the configured exposure time, saving each as a FITS frame. Disabled until a camera is connected.
CameraAcquisitionWindow.■ ABORT: Stops the running acquisition sequence after the current exposure.
CameraAcquisitionWindow.Open FITS…: Opens a previously saved FITS frame in the image viewer, for inspection alongside live acquisition.

FirstRunDialog.grating_preset: Fills the lines/mm field for this grating. The field stays editable, so any other grating can simply be typed in.
FirstRunDialog.lines_mm: Groove density of your grating in lines per mm — 100 for a Star Analyser 100, 200 for an SA200. Printed on the cell.
FirstRunDialog.distance_mm: Distance from the grating to the SENSOR, in mm. Not to the filter thread or the camera shoulder — measuring to the wrong surface is the usual reason the computed dispersion is a few percent off. Add the camera's back-focus to any spacers between grating and camera.
FirstRunDialog.pixel_um: Your camera's pixel size in microns (e.g. 3.76 for an ASI533, 2.9 for a ToUptek 585M). It is in the camera's specifications and in most FITS headers as XPIXSZ.
FirstRunDialog.result: The resulting linear dispersion in Å per pixel. Computed from the three fields above, but editable — if you already know your value, type it here directly and ignore the calculator.
FirstRunDialog.accept: Applies this dispersion to the main window and remembers your grating geometry. You can change the value at any time in the Å / px field.
